title: NVIDIA CUDA 13.5 Brings NVIDIA Vera Rubin GA Support | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: CUDA Toolkit 13.5 moves NVIDIA Vera Rubin support from early access to general availability for enterprise production and extends Windows on Arm to DGX Station for Windows. The release adds finer GPU sharing controls (locality domains, MPS v3), multi-GPU communication and SIMT interop in CUDA Tile, CCCL 3.5 features such as batched Top-K integrated into FlashInfer, and math-library speedups on Vera Rubin and Blackwell.

insights.claim: With CUDA 13.5, NVIDIA Vera Rubin support moves from early developer access to general availability, which NVIDIA describes as ready for enterprise production.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Bentz
insights.so_what: GA software support is a gating milestone for volume Vera Rubin deployments and revenue ramp.
insights.quote: NVIDIA Vera Rubin support moves from early developer access to general availability (GA), ready for enterprise production.

insights.claim: cuBLAS in CUDA 13.5 improves out-of-the-box NVFP4 and MXFP8 matmul performance on Vera Rubin, including MoE LLM training shapes, through updated heuristics and kernel tuning without per-shape autotuning.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Bentz
insights.so_what: Day-one library performance on new silicon reinforces CUDA's moat against rival accelerators.
insights.locator: Faster GEMMs on NVIDIA Vera Rubin

insights.claim: Starting with Rubin, CUDA supports only WDDM and MCDM Windows driver models; Tesla Compute Cluster (TCC) mode is not supported on Rubin and later GPUs.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Bentz
insights.so_what: Minor migration friction for Windows-based compute deployments.

insights.claim: CUDA 13.5 lets applications choose between uniform SM partitions across locality domains or partitions that include all available SMs, trading predictability for maximum hardware utilization.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Bentz
insights.so_what: Finer partitioning helps cloud providers extract more utilization from each GPU.

insights.claim: NVIDIA MPS v3 adds weighted timeslicing, SM partition borrowing and lending, cgroup v2-based routing to MPS namespaces, per-namespace SM partition assignments and polling-based memory accounting fallback.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Bentz
insights.so_what: Better multi-tenant GPU sharing supports inference-as-a-service economics on large GPUs.

themes.theme: CUDA Tile and Python programming model

insights.claim: CUDA Tile kernels can now perform multi-GPU communication directly, using unicast pointers over NVLink and multicast pointers with multimem operations on NVSwitch fabrics with NVLink SHARP, enabling fused matmul and cross-GPU reduction.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Bentz
insights.so_what: Ties higher-level programming abstractions to NVIDIA's proprietary interconnect, deepening lock-in.

insights.claim: A public preview lets cuTile Python and CUDA Tile C++ kernels call SIMT library device functions such as NVSHMEM, CCCL Coop, Warp and MathDx mid-kernel, rather than passing data through global memory across kernel boundaries.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Bentz
insights.so_what: Lowers the cost of adopting tile-based programming without abandoning existing CUDA library investments.

insights.claim: CUDA Python cuda.core 1.2 adds batched memory copies via copy_batch(), Programmatic Dependent Launch for compute capability 9.0+ GPUs, and CUDA Graph updates without reinstantiation.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Bentz
insights.so_what: Continued Python-first investment broadens CUDA's developer base.

themes.theme: Libraries for AI inference and HPC

insights.claim: CCCL 3.5 introduces cub::DeviceBatchedTopK, designed for AI workloads like token selection and sparse attention, and it is integrated into FlashInfer, a GPU kernel library for LLM inference.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Bentz
insights.so_what: Integration into widely used inference kernels shows NVIDIA embedding its primitives in the open-source LLM serving stack.

insights.claim: CCCL 3.5 adds public CUB tuning APIs, run-to-run reproducible floating-point scans, and reductions that read element counts from device memory to avoid host round-trips.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Bentz
insights.so_what: Determinism features matter for regulated and scientific users of GPU compute.

insights.claim: cuBLAS makes native FP64 symmetric updates up to 1.5x faster on NVIDIA B200 and extends the Ozaki-II scheme to FP64 symmetric rank-k updates on Ampere and newer, giving Tensor Core acceleration to Cholesky and least-squares solvers.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Bentz
insights.so_what: Emulated FP64 on Tensor Cores lets AI-oriented GPUs keep serving scientific HPC demand.

insights.claim: cuSPARSE reports 1.65x to 2.27x faster FP32/FP64 CSR SpMM with ALG3 and a new SpSV algorithm 2.7x faster than ALG1 by geometric mean, while nvJPEG hybrid decode throughput improves 10% to 600%.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Bentz
insights.so_what: Incremental software speedups extend the useful value of installed GPU fleets.

insights.claim: The Nsight Perf SDK for AI enters public preview, bringing always-on profiling to long-running training and inference workloads to diagnose intermittent performance issues.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Bentz
insights.so_what: Production observability tooling increases switching costs for large-scale CUDA users.
insights.locator: NVIDIA Nsight Perf SDK for AI

insights.claim: NVIDIA added a Compute Sanitizer agent skill to help AI coding agents choose diagnostics and interpret CUDA memory and race-condition errors, and Nsight Cloud now supports OpenTelemetry tracing for NVIDIA Dynamo deployments.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Bentz
insights.so_what: Signals NVIDIA adapting its toolchain for AI-agent-driven software development.

insights.claim: Windows on Arm support, GA since CUDA 13.4, now extends to NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows, and cuBLAS adds functional support for Blackwell GPUs including GB300 workstations on Windows on Arm.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Bentz
insights.so_what: Expands NVIDIA's reach into Arm-based Windows workstations, a nascent PC market segment.

insights.claim: A new nvprune --precompile option compiles PTX and TileIR to native SASS during packaging, eliminating runtime JIT overhead for cloud providers and package distributors targeting known architectures.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Bentz
insights.so_what: Reduces cold-start latency for cloud-deployed CUDA workloads.
